summary: Rita Langer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Hamburg in 2004 under Lambert Schmithausen and also studied at SOAS and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, later working at the University of Bristol.

Rita M. Gross (1943–2015) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned her doctorate from the University of Chicago. She taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1974–1976) and was Professor Emerita at the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire (~1979–1998).

Rizong Sras Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. Following monastic training at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950–1959), he served as Abbot of Gyume Tantric Monastery (~1979–1984), Samstanling Monastery, and Drepung Loseling Monastery (1984).

Rob Linrothe (born 1951) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Minnesota and the University of Chicago (PhD), he held academic posts at Skidmore College (1992–2009) and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

Rob Nairn (1939–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and law. Educated at the University of Zimbabwe, King's College London, and the University of Edinburgh, he held posts at the University of Zimbabwe and as professor of law and criminology at the University of Cape Town.

Robert A. F. Thurman (born 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his BA, MA, and doctorate at Harvard University. He held major posts at Amherst College (1973–1988) and as Director at Columbia University (1988–2019).
Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Texas at Austin in 2002 under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle.

Robert Alexander Neil (1852–1901) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Aberdeen and Peterhouse. He served as University Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge (1884) and as a Fellow of Pembroke College (1900).

Robert Anthony Orsi (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at Trinity College and Yale University. He held positions at Fordham, Indiana University, Harvard University (2001–2007), and Northwestern University (~2007).

Robert B. Ekvall (1898–1983) was an anthropologist and Tibetologist. He served as a research associate at the University of Chicago (~1953–1957), a research fellow at the University of Washington (1958), and honorary curator at the Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture.

Robert Baker Aitken (1917–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at the University of Hawaiʻi and UC Berkeley, he studied Zen under various teachers in Japan and the US, and held posts at the East-West Center and University of Hawaiʻi.

Robert Barnett (born 1953) is a Tibetology scholar educated at the University of Cambridge. He served as Adjunct Professor and Senior Research Scholar at Columbia University (~1999–2018) and later as Professorial Research Associate at SOAS University of London (~2018).

Robert Buswell (born 1953) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his AB, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley under teachers including Lewis Lancaster. He served as a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1993–2022).

Robert Caesar Childers (1838–1876) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Wadham College, Oxford. He served as Sub-Librarian at the India Office (1872) and Professor of Pali and Buddhist literature at University College London (~1872–1876).

Robert Chalmers (1858–1938) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oriel College, Oxford, under T. W. Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922–1925) and Master of Peterhouse (1924–1931).

Sir Robert Chambers (1737–1803) was a legal scholar and Indologist educated at Lincoln College, Oxford. He served as Vinerian Professor of English Law at Oxford (1766), Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William (~1789–1798), and president of The Asiatic Society (~1797–1798).

Robert Charles Zaehner (1913–1974) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Iranian studies who studied at Christ Church and Cambridge under H. W. Bailey. He was Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics at Oxford and a fellow of All Souls College (~1952–1974).

Robert DeCaroli (born 1970) is a scholar of history, art history, and Buddhist studies who earned his MA and PhD from UCLA under Robert L. Brown. He taught at UCLA and Loyola Marymount before joining the faculty at George Mason University (~2004).

Robert Deliège (born 1953) is an anthropologist and scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford (~1980–1985). He has served as a professor at the Université catholique de Louvain since ~1989.

Robert Duquenne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has been affiliated with Hōbōgirin as a specialist in Tantric Buddhism (attested 1981) and with the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).
